title: Streaming fragment reassembler and typed-event surface for Python SDK
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: In long-running streaming chat sessions we frequently observe tokens and structured events arriving split across transport boundaries (SSE/frame/chunk). This makes it hard for application code to consume atomic semantic events (e.g., function_call start/arg fragments, structured JSON patches, tool call boundaries) and to support idempotent resume after retries or reconnects.

Goal: Implement a resilient fragment reassembly layer and a typed streaming-event surface in the Python SDK that: 1) reassembles delimited/fragmented payloads (token fragments, JSON fragments, function_call arg fragments), 2) yields strongly-typed events (Delta, Fragment, Patch, FunctionStart, FunctionArg, FunctionEnd, Done, Error), 3) exposes checkpoint tokens and resume semantics to enable safe retries and reconnects, 4) emits telemetry for fragmentation metrics and reassembly latency, and 5) keeps the developer ergonomics simple (async iterator + optional callbacks).

This ticket covers: design, prototype implementation, unit + integration tests against the streaming test harness, and a small migration guide for existing customers who use raw streaming byte handlers.
acceptance_criteria: SDK exposes StreamSession.async_events() async-generator that yields typed events and checkpoint markers
Reassembly handles fragments split at arbitrary boundaries (including mid-UTF8 and mid-JSON-token) without data loss
Resume token semantics enable at-most-once or at-least-once per-caller choice documented in the API
Telemetry: metrics for fragmented-message-rate, average-reassembly-latency, resume-success-rate
End-to-end integration test against streaming-test-harness covers function_call across 3 fragment boundaries
proposed_api_snippet:
# Example async usage
from redwood_sdk import StreamSession, EventType

async with StreamSession(model="redwood-small-chat") as session:
    async for ev in session.async_events():
        if ev.type == EventType.DELTA:
            print(ev.text, end="")
        elif ev.type == EventType.FUNCTION_START:
            current_fn = ev.name
        elif ev.type == EventType.FUNCTION_ARG:
            # arguments may arrive fragmented; ev.fragment_id groups parts
            arguments_buffer.append(ev.payload)
        elif ev.type == EventType.FUNCTION_END:
            args = "".join(arguments_buffer)
            handle_function_call(current_fn, args)
        elif ev.type == EventType.CHECKPOINT:
            # store resume token externally
            persist_resume_token(ev.token)
implementation_notes: Transport-agnostic reassembly: layer works with SSE, chunked HTTP, and framed RPC by normalizing incoming byte frames to (offset, bytes) input
Use an incremental UTF-8 safe concat with state machine for JSON/object token detection to avoid invalid sequences
Assign fragment_id for logical message and part_index for ordering; keep small in-memory sliding-window per-session (bounded to 1MB by default)
Checkpoint tokens include session_id + last_event_seq + per-fragment-ack bitmap (encoded compactly)
Provide two resume modes: 'soft' (idempotent replay; duplicates may be coalesced by caller) and 'strict' (server-side resume where already-acked tokens are not re-sent if supported)
Backpressure: expose awaitable drain() helper and optional max_buffer_size to avoid unbounded buffering on slow consumers
Metrics: increment fragmented_message_count, fragment_reassembly_failures, resume_attempts, resume_successes
Security: resume token contains a short HMAC to prevent token forging; tokens rotate per-session
testing_plan: Unit tests for reassembly state machine with fuzzed arbitrary split points (including mid-UTF8 codepoint)
Integration test that runs streaming-test-harness injecting splits at multiple points and verifies event ordering and complete JSON payload reconstruction
Chaos test: simulate reconnect and retry using persisted checkpoint token and assert idempotent outcome for at-least-once flows
Performance microbench: measure average reassembly latency under 1000 concurrent sessions and ensure < 1ms added CPU overhead per event on p4d
E2E example script in examples/python/streaming_reassembly_demo.py that developers can run locally
risks_and_mitigations: Memory blow-up if a malicious stream never finishes a fragment — mitigation: per-session sliding-window + fragment TTL + circuit-breaker that fails session after threshold
Resume semantics mismatch with older server versions — mitigation: version-guard in resume token and fallback to full-stream re-fetch
Increased SDK complexity harming ergonomics — mitigation: provide high-level async_events() default and low-level Reassembler API for advanced uses
rollout_plan: Feature gated behind runtime flag 'python_stream_reassembly' and opt-in in SDK 1.21.0-beta
Ship in beta to 10 internal customers and ~20% of hosted traffic behind a flag for 2 weeks
Collect telemetry and error rates, revert or iterate if fragmented_message_failure_rate > 0.1%
Promote to GA with migration guide and changelog entry after two successful cycles
